Car-free cities are becoming increasingly popular, as governments and urban planners seek to address the negative impact of cars on the environment and public health. In this essay, we will explore the benefits of car-free cities and discuss the challenges that must be overcome to create a successful car-free urban environment. One of the main benefits of car-free cities is improved air quality. Cars are a significant source of pollution, and reducing their numbers in urban areas can lead to a dramatic improvement in air quality. In addition to the health benefits, reducing air pollution can also have economic benefits, as it can lead to lower healthcare costs for residents and higher productivity due to fewer sick days. Car-free cities also offer many other benefits, such as increased safety, reduced noise pollution, and greater access to public transportation and bicycles. They allow for the creation of more green spaces in the city and offer ample opportunities for walking, cycling, and other outdoor activities. However, creating a car-free city is not without its challenges. One of the biggest challenges is finding alternative modes of transportation for those who cannot walk or cycle. This requires investment in public transportation and other alternative modes of transport, such as electric vehicles or bicycle-sharing programs. Another challenge is the need to reconfigure urban spaces to accommodate a reduced reliance on cars. This includes the creation of bike lanes and pedestrian-friendly streets, as well as the integration of parking garages and other car parking facilities. In conclusion, car-free cities offer many benefits, including improved air quality, increased safety, and greater access to green spaces and outdoor activities. However, creating a successful car-free urban environment requires significant investment in alternative modes of transportation and the reconfiguration of urban spaces. While the challenges may be substantial, the benefits of car-free cities make them a worthwhile pursuit.

We address scene layout modeling for recognizing agent-in-place actions, which are actions associated with agents who perform them and the places where they occur, in the context of outdoor home scenes. We evaluate how these modelers learn to design a plausible physical mapping from the view locations of an agent's camera to its corresponding input location on the screen (i.e., the virtual control point). The goal is then to set up a system that can automatically recognize the presence of an agent at any given place in the virtual space; the scenario we propose here was not previously explored by anyone. In this paper, we study scene layout modelling (SLM) and present a framework for considering comprehensive views to the environment instead of only local ones that might be seen directly from within a single room or window. SLMs were described in cite14. While this work focuses mainly on indoor environments, it should have application to many other scenarios as well. In particular, our approach will help designers to consider multiple viewpoints when designing the building structure, such as new buildings designed after earthquakes and more recently after terrorist attacks [1]. It signals whether something has changed since the last time the designer visited that area. This provides an important information about the consequences of recent events and therefore can aid the designer in planning for future improvements and preventive measures [2]. An uplink system with a single antenna transmitter and a single receiver with a large number of antennas is considered. We propose an energy-detection-based single-shot noncoherent communication scheme which does not use the instantaneous channel state information (CSI), but rather only the knowledge of the channel statistics. The suggested system uses a transmitter that modulates information on the power of the symbols, and a receiver which measures only the average energy across the antennas. We propose constellation designs which are asymptotically optimal with respect to symbol error rate (SER) with an increasing number of antennas, for any finite signal to noise ratio (SNR) at the receiver, under different assumptions on the availability of CSI statistics (exact channel fading distribution or the first few moments of the channel fading distribution). We also consider the case of imperfect knowledge of the channel statistics and describe in detail the case when there is a bounded uncertainty on the moments of the fading distribution. We present numerical results on the SER performance achieved by these designs in typical scenarios and find that they may outperform existing noncoherent constellations, e.g., conventional Amplitude Shift Keying (ASK), and pilot-based schemes, e.g., Pulse Amplitude Modulation (PAM). We also observe that an optimized constellation for a specific channel distribution makes it very sensitive to uncertainties in the channel statistics. In particular, constellation designs based on optimistic channel conditions could lead to significant performance degradation in terms of the achieved symbol error rates.

Tyson Fury's Chaotic Reign as World Heavyweight Champion For many boxing fans, Tyson Fury's reign as heavyweight champion of the world was one of the most chaotic and unpredictable periods in recent memory. The larger-than-life British boxer became a household name thanks to his antics both in and out of the ring, with his eccentric personality and bombastic trash talking entertaining fans and frustrating opponents in equal measure. Despite the chaos that often surrounded him, however, Fury's reign as world champion was strangely predictable. From the moment he won the title with an upset victory over Wladimir Klitschko in 2015, Fury seemed almost destined to fall from grace. His stunning victory over the long-reigning champion was followed by a period of self-destructive behavior that saw him spiral into addiction, depression, and self-harm. As he battled his demons, Fury struggled to stay in shape and keep up with the sport's other top contenders. He vacated his titles and went into self-imposed exile, withdrawing from the sport for over two years. During this time, he was stripped of his various belts, and most boxing insiders assumed he would never fight again. But in 2018, Fury made a dramatic return to the sport, shedding over 100 pounds and re-committing himself to his training. Despite being out of the ring for so long, he quickly reclaimed his status as one of the sport's top competitors. He fought to a controversial draw against Deontay Wilder in his first title fight since returning, and then won a decision in their rematch the following year. Throughout his career, Fury has always been a polarizing figure. His brash personality, unusual training methods, and outright bizarre behavior have made him a target of criticism from many boxing traditionalists. But even his harshest critics must admit that there is something unique and fascinating about Fury's story. For a man who has been described as capricious and unpredictable, Tyson Fury's reign as world heavyweight champion was strangely predictable. His journey has been marked by highs and lows, moments of triumph and moments of despair. But through it all, Fury has remained one of the sport's most captivating and enduring figures - a champion in every sense of the word.

A reverse mortgage is a type of loan that allows homeowners who are 62 years of age or older to borrow money using their home as collateral. The loan is called a "reverse" mortgage because the homeowner does not have to make monthly payments to the lender. Instead, the lender makes payments to the homeowner, and the loan becomes due when the homeowner sells the house, moves out of the house, or passes away. To get a reverse mortgage, the homeowner must own their home outright or have a low mortgage balance that can be paid off with the reverse mortgage. The lender will then determine how much money the homeowner is eligible to borrow based on the value of their home and the homeowner's age. The homeowner can choose to receive the money from the reverse mortgage in a lump sum, as a line of credit, or as monthly payments. The homeowner is still responsible for paying property taxes and homeowners insurance, and for maintaining the home in good condition. If the homeowner sells the house or moves out, they or their estate will need to repay the reverse mortgage, plus interest and any fees that have accumulated over time. If the sale of the house does not cover the amount owed on the reverse mortgage, the homeowner or their estate will not be responsible for paying the difference.

In this paper, we study the waveform design problem for a single-input single-output (SISO) radio-frequency (RF) wireless power transfer (WPT) system in frequency-selective channels. First, based on the actual non-linear ities of the system that are inherent to SISO systems and can be neglected, an optimal low-complexity solution is obtained using finite difference time domain methods without modeling the non-linearities explicitly; then the performance of our optimization algorithm is evaluated by simulation studies at different additive white Gaussian noise (AWGN) channel conditions. For these simulations, the random amplitude variation coefficient with bandwidth b 10 MHz is used as initial seed value, with 100 ms sampling interval and with constant AWGN level of 0 dBmMHz. The results show that our proposed method achieves better than 95 average efficiency, which is sufficient to meet the commercial requirements of WPT applications. This article proposes two new schemes called shift register pulse shaping (SRPS) and random cross-correlation pulse shaping (RCPS). Both SRPS and RCPS use the same basic idea: they first multiply the input signal by a complex function allowing them to use only one phase rotation component of each sample. This makes their scalability more efficient than standard digital-to-analog converter pulse shaping algorithms because it eliminates the multipliers needed by analog implementations. Then, both SRPS and RCPS convert the result into the required baseband analog shape using simple subtractor circuits, similar to those used in conventional digital filters. Finally, they add quantization error corrections using hardware circuit elements and perform some additional processing like filtering and amplification before outputting the original signal. All the components of the final processing chain are implemented entirely within dedicated programmable logic devices (PLDs), such as field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs) or application specific integrated circuits (ASICs). One example implementation is presented and tested using the Xilinx Virtex II FPGA family. Results show that these two methods achieve comparable improvements over existing techniques while requiring significantly less area and power consumption.

The art of bookbinding has evolved tremendously over many centuries. Bookbinding began as a practical craft, a means of preserving and protecting loose papers and parchments. As books became more widespread, bookbinding developed into an artistic endeavor in its own right. Bookbinding originated in the 2nd century AD with the rise of the codex, an early form of the modern book. The codex replaced scrolls and allowed for the collection of multiple writings into a single bound volume. These early codices were made of folded parchment or papyrus sheets stitched together at the spine. Covers made of leather, wood, or ivory were added for protection. As parchment and paper became more available and less expensive, bookbinding grew into an art form. In the 15th century, the printing press allowed for mass production of books. This proliferation of books spurred new innovations in bookbinding. New decorative techniques were developed, including gold tooling, embossing, and stamping. Bindings were made from luxurious materials like leather, velvet, and silk. Clasps and straps were added to keep books closed when not in use. During the Industrial Revolution, mechanization transformed bookbinding. New machines could cut, fold, and stitch signatures (groups of pages) at high speeds. Decorative cloth and leather bindings were mass produced. Although these machine-made books were more affordable and available to the general public, many bookbinders lamented the decline of traditional hand binding techniques. In the 20th century, fine bookbinding experienced a revival as an art form. Hand bookbinders employed traditional techniques with new artistic sensibilities. Bound books became works of art in themselves, using unusual and striking materials and designs. Contemporary bookbinders incorporate found materials, mixed media, and digital technologies into their bindings. While e-books and digital publishing have challenged the role of physical books, the art of fine bookbinding persists and continues to evolve. In conclusion, bookbinding has a rich and varied history spanning over 1,800 years. What began as a practical means of compiling writings has developed into an artistic tradition in its own right. Despite periods of mechanization, hand bookbinding has endured, preserved, and advanced by artisans and artists who value the bound book as an object of beauty. The art of bookbinding will undoubtedly continue to evolve as long as there are those who appreciate the bound book as an artistic and cultural artifact.

Starting from this intuition, we propose a novel approach to compose representations learned by different components in neural machine translation (e.g., multi-layer networks or multi-head attention), based on modeling strong interactions among neurons in the representation vectors. Specifically, we leverage bilinear pooling to model pairwise multiplicative interactions among individual neurons, and a low-rank approximation to make the model computationally feasible. We further propose extended bilinear pooling to incorporate first-order representations. Experiments on WMT14 English German and English French translation tasks show that our model consistently improves performances over the SOTA Transformer baseline. Further analyses demonstrate that our approach indeed captures more syntactic and semantic information as expected.

Industrialized societies generally follow a clock-based schedule for daily activities that do not change throughout the course of the year. The time of day that individuals begin and end work or school, and the coordination of mass transit, for example, usually remain constant year-round. In contrast, an agrarian society's daily routines for work and personal conduct are more likely governed by the length of daylight hours and by solar time, which change seasonally because of the Earth's axial tilt. North and south of the tropics daylight lasts longer in summer and shorter in winter, the effect becoming greater as one moves away from the tropics.

Machine learning models are shown to be vulnerable to adversarial examples. While most of the existing methods for adversarial attack and defense work on 2D image domains, a few recent works demonstrate that 3D models are also susceptible to adversarial perturbation. However, the image-based attacks are no longer applicable in 3D domains due to the inherent differences between images and 3D objects. This paper presents a framework to generate adversarial perturbations for 3D models using geometric transformations. Our experiments on multiple 3D classification tasks demonstrate the vulnerability of various 3D models, as well as the superiority of our attack framework compared with the existing 3D-based attacks.

Classification of HEp-2 cell patterns plays a significant role in the indirect immunofluorescence test for identifying autoimmune diseases in the human body. Many automatic HEp-2 cell classification methods have been proposed in recent years, amongst which deep learning based methods have shown impressive performance. This paper provides a comprehensive review of the existing deep learning based HEp-2 cell image classification methods. These methods perform HEp-2 image classification at two levels, namely, cell-level and specimen-level. Both levels are covered in this review. At each level, the methods are organized with a deep network usage based taxonomy. The core idea, notable achievements, and key strengths and weaknesses of each method are critically analyzed. Furthermore, a concise review of the existing HEp-2 datasets that are commonly used in the literature is given. The paper ends with a discussion on novel opportunities and future research directions in this field. It is hoped that this paper would provide readers with a thorough reference of this novel, challenging, and thriving field.

A number of decoy towns were constructed in Somerset in World War II to protect Bristol and other towns, at night. They were designed to mimic the geometry of "blacked out" streets, railway lines, and Bristol Temple Meads railway station, to encourage bombers away from these targets. One, on the radio beam flight path to Bristol, was constructed on Beacon Batch. It was laid out by Shepperton Studios, based on aerial photographs of the city's railway marshalling yards. The decoys were fitted with dim red lights, simulating activities like the stoking of steam locomotives. Burning bales of straw soaked in creosote were used to simulate the effects of incendiary bombs dropped by the first wave of Pathfinder night bombers; meanwhile, incendiary bombs dropped on the correct location were quickly smothered, wherever possible. Drums of oil were also ignited to simulate the effect of a blazing city or town, with the aim of fooling subsequent waves of bombers into dropping their bombs on the wrong location. The Chew Magna decoy town was hit by half-a-dozen bombs on 2 December 1940, and over a thousand incendiaries on 3 January 1941. The following night the Uphill decoy town, protecting Weston-super-Mare's airfield, was bombed; a herd of dairy cows was hit, killing some and severely injuring others.

We study the problem of allocating a set of indivisible goods to multiple agents. Recent work focused on allocating goods in a sequential way, and studied what is the "best" sequence of agents to pick objects based on utilitarian or egalitarian criterion. In this paper, we propose a parallel elicitation-free protocol for allocating indivisible goods. In every round of the allocation process, some agents will be selected (according to some policy) to report their preferred objects among those that remain, and every reported object will be allocated randomly to an agent reporting it. Empirical comparison between the parallel protocol (applying a simple selection policy) and the sequential protocol (applying the optimal sequence) reveals that our proposed protocol is promising. We also address strategical issues.

Special procedures apply to legislation passed by Tynwald, the legislature of the Isle of Man. Before the lordship of the Island was purchased by the British Crown in 1765 (the Revestment), the assent of the Lord of Mann to a bill was signified by letter to the governor. new.css is a classless CSS framework that can write modern websites using only HTML. It features a dark mode and support for custom color themes and fonts using CSS variables. Founder Erik Brunner revealed in 2018 that he was working on the project during his free time, but had no idea at all what it would look like when finished. He did not even know how many people were building web apps with his work. In fact, some of them built Facebook Messenger's News Feed after seeing an earlier version of New.CSS on HackerNews back then. Nevertheless, he continued to work on the platform as most people kept showing interest in bringing him up-to speed with its usage. Though Brunner admits that he sometimes "startles" himself by realizing just how long ago this started: It's been almost two years since I've stopped coding New.CSS - wow! Two whole years... The reason we're doing this now instead of before or something else has nothing to do with any particular tech feature (we have those too). We wanted to get everyone who'd ever asked us about New.CSS into one place where they could know if there are others out there using our work:) The patch below removes copyright notice from the top right corner seal box so anyone hosting their own copy will see this also applies to them. If you want to be sure someone got your releases early please add a newline between '.' and your email address. The latest release comes exactly three weeks ahead of something similar called Styled Components. Last month, I described both platforms as being very similar to each other except one focuses more on styling while the other does not care much about styles as much anymore due to Web Component adoption. In Conclusion Final Thoughts Though you might think New.CSS is incredibly old news by comparison to both Styled Components and Polymer, which debuted less than five months later, it still deserves attention because of its simplicity and ability to create highly responsive sites without JavaScript libraries or frameworks. First impressions are a powerful tool in shaping our perceptions of others. While some people believe that they can control their first impressions at any time, the reality is that first impressions are often formed quickly and unconsciously. These initial impressions can be difficult to change, depending on the situation and the individual's emotional state. One of the most significant ways that first impressions can impact our lives is through their ability to affect our behavior. For example, if someone has a negative first impression of another person, they may be more likely to behave in a hostile or confrontational manner towards that person. On the other hand, if someone has a positive first impression, they may be more likely to approach the person with warmth and friendliness. The emotions that we experience during our first impressions can also have a lasting impact on our relationships with others. The senate has a bunch of self-imposed rules that exist for various reasons. These rules aren't described by the constitution, and can be changed by the majority party in the senate. One of big rules is the filibuster, which basically allows the minority side to hold up the voting process on billsnominationsetc. so that they can't be passed. The idea is to avoid the "tyranny of the majority" on really big issues. The majority party has generally left this option available, with the understanding that the minority party would only use it in situations where they had a really substantial objection to a given billnominationetc. The "nuclear option" would be the majority party changing the senate rules to reduce or remove the power of the filibuster. It gets brought up whenever the majority party feels like the minority side is abusing the filibuster power, holding up minor things, or using filibusters on particular issues to try and force changes on unrelated bills or whatever. It's given the scary name of the "nuclear option" because it would be a significant change of how the senate has worked. On one hand it sounds like a no-brainer for the majority, who'd be able to pass whatever the hell they wanted assuming they could get 51 votes. But the flip side is that it's tough to guarantee that you'll still be the majority after the next election, and do you really want to hand that unchecked majority power to the other side if they end up the majority next time?

Painting captions are often dry and simplistic which motivates us to describe a painting creatively in the style of Shakespearean prose. This is a difficult problem, since there does not exist a large supervised dataset from paintings to Shakespearean prose. Our solution is to use an intermediate English poem description of the painting and then apply language style transfer which results in Shakespearean prose describing the painting. Drivers should not be allowed to use cell phones in any capacity while operating a vehicle. While cell phones have become an integral part of modern life, they present a serious distraction when used behind the wheel. Numerous studies have shown that cell phone use while driving can impair a driver as much as having a blood alcohol level over the legal limit. Drivers engaged in phone conversations have slower reaction times, miss traffic signals and signs more often, and have a greater chance of being involved in an accident. This is because using a phone, whether it's hands-free or handheld, requires the driver's visual attention to be diverted from the road and their cognitive workload to increase. Answering calls, sending texts, or scrolling through social media all take the driver's focus away from their primary task of safely operating the vehicle. Proponents of allowing limited cell phone use argue that hands-free devices are safer than handheld phones. However, research indicates this is a misconception. The cognitive distraction of engaging in a phone conversation is still present whether the phone is handheld or not. A driver is processing and formulating responses to the person on the other end of the line, taking their mind off watching the road and other vehicles. This places all other drivers and pedestrians at risk of an accident. Some also claim that adults should have the freedom to choose whether to use their phone or not. However, a car is not Must a personal space but rather a deadly weapon that endangers others if not operated carefully. When lives are at stake, the responsibility lies with lawmakers to prioritize public safety over personal convenience. Comprehensive bans on cell phone use while driving have been shown to reduce accidents and injuries in many Jurisdictions. In conclusion, the dangers of cell phone distracted driving are well substantiated. Even hands-free use diverts drivers' attention from their primary task and elevates collision risks. For the sake of protecting all road users, cell phones should not be used by drivers under any circumstance when a vehicle is in motion. Strict laws are needed to discourage this risky behavior and make our roads safer for everyone.

The Christie treats more than 40,000 patients a year, with about a quarter of patients referred from other parts of the country for specialist treatment. Blockchain technology is a distributed database that is used to maintain a continuously growing list of records, called blocks. This technology has the potential to revolutionize many industries, including supply chain management. In supply chain management, blockchain technology can be used to track the movement of goods from the point of origin to the point of sale. This can provide a number of benefits, including increased transparency, efficiency, and security. Increased transparency is one of the most important benefits of using blockchain technology in supply chain management. Blockchain provides a tamper-proof record of all transactions, which can help to build trust between buyers and sellers. For example, a buyer can use blockchain to verify that the product they are purchasing is authentic and has not been tampered with. This can help to reduce fraud and protect consumers from counterfeit products. Efficiency is another important benefit of using blockchain technology in supply chain management. Blockchain can help to streamline the flow of information and goods throughout the supply chain. For example, blockchain can be used to track the location of goods in real-time, which can help to improve inventory management and reduce shipping costs. Additionally, blockchain can be used to automate payments, which can save time and money. Security is another important benefit of using blockchain technology in supply chain management. Blockchain is a secure and tamper-proof way to store data. This can help to protect sensitive information, such as financial data and customer information, from being accessed by unauthorized parties. Additionally, blockchain can be used to track the movement of goods and ensure that they are not stolen or tampered with. Overall, blockchain technology has the potential to revolutionize supply chain management. This technology can provide a number of benefits, including increased transparency, efficiency, and security. As blockchain technology continues to develop, it is likely to play an increasingly important role in the supply chain management industry.

In this paper, we propose a characterization of chordal bipartite graphs and an efficient enumeration algorithm for chordal bipartite induced subgraphs. A chordal bipartite graph is a bipartite graph without induced cycles with length six or more. It is known that the incident graph of a hypergraph is chordal bipartite graph if and only if the hypergraph is b -acyclic. As the main result of our paper, we show that a graph G is chordal bipartite if and only if there is a special vertex elimination ordering for G, called CBEO. Moreover, we propose an algorithm ECB which enumerates all chordal bipartite induced subgraphs in O (k t D 2) time per solution on average, where k is the degeneracy, t is the maximum size of K t, t as an induced subgraph, and D is the degree. ECB achieves constant amortized time enumeration for bounded degree graphs.

The old, dilapidated warehouse towered before me as I walked down the abandoned street. Every window was shattered, the brick exterior crumbling and covered in graffiti. It had an eerie, haunted quality that both frightened and intrigued me. I knew I shouldn't enter - the building was condemned and structurally unsafe. But my curiosity got the better of me. I walked up to the large metal front doors, rusted and hanging off their hinges, and slowly entered the musty darkness within. My flashlight flickered on, illuminating the cavernous space. An old reception desk stood covered in decades of dust. Filing cabinets were tipped over, their contents spilled across the floor and yellowed with age. As I ventured deeper, my footsteps echoed through the emptiness. I began to notice odd details - a single high heeled shoe lying in a corner, a vintage coat still hanging on a hook, a faded advertisement on one wall. It was as if the people who once worked here vanished instantly, leaving everything behind. The eeriness intensified. I walked through a set of double doors into what looked like an old laboratory. Beakers and test tubes were scattered across tables, some still holding mysterious liquids. An antique microscope sat by a ledger, as if someone was in the middle of examining a specimen. But where did they go? It was a perfectly preserved snapshot of the past, a place trapped in time. My heart began to race as my imagination spun out of control. What happened here? I thought I heard a faint sound in the distance. I whipped around, flashlight searching the darkness, but couldn't see anything. The feeling of being watched crept over me. I quickened my pace, no longer curious but desperate to escape this haunted place. I finally found my way out of the maze of rooms and back to the front entrance. With a huge sense of relief, I emerged into the sunlight and left the warehouse behind. As much as I love discovering forgotten places, there are some doors that should remain unopened, some secrets better left undisturbed. I was happy to put as much distance as possible between myself and that strange, unsettling portal to the past.

Polarimetric synthetic aperture radar (PolSAR) image segmentation is currently of great importance in image processing for remote sensing applications. However, it is a challenging task due to two main reasons. Firstly the small pixel size and secondly the presence of false color artifacts inherent to satellite imagery used as input data set. We propose an ant-based algorithm which directly associates pixels with their nearest neighbors in order to reduce false color effects but also exploits redundancy at both scale and range using nonlinear projection onto convex sets (NPC). The long-standing byzantine agreement problem gets more attention in recent years due to the increasing demand for scalable geo-replicated Byzantine state machine replication (SMR) systems (e.g., Blockchains). To date, the only solution proposed is a clever combination of optimistic and pessimistic locking techniques that allows concurrent access to a replicated SMR system while ensuring consensus (collaboration between all participants) at the same time. This paper presents two different implementations using the new atomic BroadcastLock interface and proposes an improved method based on its use which provides superior throughput. In this work we propose Atomic BroadcastLocks as a general data structure capable of implementing multiple concurrent locks without performance degradation. We first consider atomically broadcasted messages, then blocks of transactions with various ordering constraints and finally a large number of conflicting writes in parallel to achieve better concurrency control when doing atomic operations against shared memory resources. The algorithm itself can be thought of as a form of lock-free programming paradigm, where each part of the expression uses atomic primitives like CompareAndSet and WriteMultiplier together with efficient mechanisms like MVCC or lock delegation to keep track of the current execution status from one step to another. In particular comparing two numbers has been shown to offer no overhead over performing sequential reads even if the compare operation involves an expensive load operation.

The world of finance is on the cusp of a transformative era, driven by the inexorable rise of cryptocurrencies. These digital currencies, operating on decentralized networks, have the potential to revolutionize the way we perceive and conduct financial transactions. Unlike traditional fiat currencies, cryptocurrencies are not subject to the control of central banks or governments, offering users unprecedented autonomy and security. The decentralized nature of cryptocurrencies eliminates the need for intermediaries, reducing transaction costs and increasing efficiency. This democratization of finance enables individuals and businesses to engage in direct peer-to-peer transactions, fostering greater financial inclusion and accessibility. Furthermore, the immutability of blockchain technology, the underlying infrastructure of cryptocurrencies, ensures the integrity and transparency of transactions, minimizing the risk of fraud and corruption. One of the most significant advantages of cryptocurrencies lies in their borderless nature. Unlike traditional currencies, which are subject to geographical restrictions and currency exchange rates, cryptocurrencies can be seamlessly transferred across borders without incurring substantial fees. This facilitates global commerce and remittances, empowering individuals and businesses to engage in international transactions with greater ease and affordability. Moreover, cryptocurrencies provide a hedge against inflation, a persistent challenge in traditional financial systems. Their limited supply and decentralized nature make them immune to the devaluation risks associated with fiat currencies. As a result, cryptocurrencies serve as a store of value, offering investors a potential safeguard against economic uncertainties. However, it is essential to acknowledge the inherent risks associated with cryptocurrencies. Their decentralized nature can make them susceptible to volatility and price fluctuations, leading to potential losses for investors. Additionally, the lack of regulation in some jurisdictions can create opportunities for illicit activities, such as money laundering and terrorist financing. Despite these challenges, the potential benefits of cryptocurrencies far outweigh the risks. As the technology matures and regulatory frameworks evolve, cryptocurrencies are poised to play an increasingly pivotal role in shaping the future of financial transactions. Their decentralized, secure, and borderless nature has the power to revolutionize the way we manage our finances, fostering greater financial inclusion, efficiency, and resilience in the global financial system.

We outline a detection method for adversarial inputs to deep neural networks. Our method is simple, scalable, and can detect inputs that fool deep neural networks of any architecture and can be applied to any task.

The Facial Action Coding System (FACS) is an innovative tool that can analyze human emotions and has been demonstrated by analyzing the enigmatic smile of Leonardo da Vinci's Mona Lisa. The article raises concerns about the effectiveness of the FACS system in classrooms, where teachers already possess the ability to sense and respond to student emotions effectively. The author argues that the human brain naturally performs complex emotional calculations, and emotion-detecting software is unnecessary in environments where human interaction is key. This perspective challenges the need for such technology in educational settings. Moreover, the deployment of emotion recognition software in classrooms raises profound privacy concerns. The FACS system, while advanced in recognizing emotions like confusion or boredom, lacks the capacity to understand the underlying causes of these emotions. In a diverse classroom setting, students bring a myriad of personal experiences and emotions that may not be directly related to the classroom environment. The application of emotion detection technology in such a setting could lead to invasive scrutiny of students' private emotional states, potentially exacerbating their distress. Additionally, the potential benefits of personalized learning experiences through emotion detection technology are overshadowed by practical and financial constraints. The implementation of personalized emotion-detecting computers for each student would entail significant financial investments, making it an impractical solution for most educational institutions. In conclusion, while the concept of computers understanding and responding to human emotions is fascinating, its application in educational settings raises privacy and practicality concerns. The article emphasizes the importance of human-centric teaching methods and the need to approach technological integration in education with caution and respect for privacy. As the age of technology progresses, it becomes crucial to remember the value of human touch in education, a realm where emotional understanding and connection are paramount.

Ethereum has emerged as the most popular smart contract development platform, with hundreds of thousands of contracts stored on the blockchain and covering a variety of application scenarios, such as auctions, trading platforms, and so on. Given their financial nature, security vulnerabilities may lead to catastrophic consequences and, even worse, they can be hardly fixed as data stored on the blockchain, including the smart contract code itself, are immutable. An automated security analysis of these contracts is thus of utmost interest, but at the same time technically challenging for a variety of reasons, such as the specific transaction-oriented programming mechanisms, which feature a subtle semantics, and the fact that the blockchain data which the contract under analysis interacts with, including the code of callers and callees, are not statically known. In this work, we present eThor , the first sound and automated static analyzer for EVM bytecode, which is based on an abstraction of the EVM bytecode semantics based on Horn clauses. In particular, our static analysis supports reachability properties, which we show to be sufficient for capturing interesting security properties for smart contracts (e.g., single-entrancy) as well as contract-specific functional properties. Our analysis is proven sound against a complete semantics of EVM bytecode and an experimental large-scale evaluation on real-world contracts demonstrates that eThor is practical and outperforms the state-of-the-art static analyzers: specifically, eThor is the only one to provide soundness guarantees, terminates on 95 of a representative set of real-world contracts, and achieves an F -measure (which combines sensitivity and specificity) of 89.

Facial Action Coding System (FACS) is a technique used by researchers to analyze and decode the facial movements and expressions of individuals. It is an interdisciplinary approach that combines anatomy, psychology, and neuroscience to understand the complex communication and emotions that are conveyed through the face. FACS is based on the idea that facial movements are not random, but rather are patterned and systematic. Researchers have identified a set of basic facial movements or actions that are used to create a wide range of expressions, such as smiling, frowning, and raising eyebrows. These actions are coded into a system that allows researchers to decode the specific emotions or states of mind that are expressed by an individual. The FACS technique involves the use of cameras and software to record the movements of the facial muscles. The data collected is then analyzed using a set of predefined codes to identify the specific actions that are being used. This allows researchers to gain insight into the underlying mechanisms of emotion and communication, and to understand how different emotions are conveyed through the face. One of the applications of FACS is in the field of neuroscience. Researchers have used the technique to study the neural mechanisms underlying emotion and decision-making. By analyzing the facial expressions of individuals, researchers can gain insight into the activation of specific regions of the brain that are associated with different emotions and states of mind. FACS also has practical applications in fields such as marketing and advertising. By understanding how different facial expressions convey different emotions, companies can design more effective advertising and marketing campaigns that are better able to influence consumer behavior. In conclusion, FACS is a powerful tool for understanding the complex communication and emotions that are conveyed through the face. By analyzing facial movements and expressions, researchers can gain insight into the underlying mechanisms of emotion and decision-making, and develop more effective strategies for communicating and influencing behavior.

It is not inevitable that we will completely run out of helium, but it is important to use it responsibly and to find ways to recycle and reuse it to help conserve this valuable resource.

The Welch Bound is a lower bound on the root mean square cross correlation between n unit-norm vectors f 1 , ... , f n in the m dimensional space (R m or C m), for n m . Letting F [ f 1 ... f n ] denote the m -by- n frame matrix, the Welch bound can be viewed as a lower bound on the second moment of F , namely on the trace of the squared Gram matrix ( F F) 2 . We consider an erasure setting, in which a reduced frame, composed of a random subset of Bernoulli selected vectors, is of interest. We extend the Welch bound to this setting and present the erasure Welch bound on the expected value of the Gram matrix of the reduced frame. Interestingly, this bound generalizes to the d -th order moment of F . We provide simple, explicit formulae for the generalized bound for d 2 , 3 , 4 , which is the sum of the d -th moment of Wachter's classical MANOVA distribution and a vanishing term (as n goes to infinity with m n held constant). The bound holds with equality if (and for d 4 only if) F is an Equiangular Tight Frame (ETF). Our results offer a novel perspective on the superiority of ETFs over other frames in a variety of applications, including spread spectrum communications, compressed sensing and analog coding.

As the liquid escapes it loses contact with the vessel . Through a process called adhesion the water in your product will experience a drag effect as the contact with the waste channel is extinguished . This drag is greatest in areas that contain the most perturbation . The shape of the orifice that produces the stream produces the vast majority of the perturbative influence . In this case the opening is a slit which produces semi - toroidal flows in the medium at the polar vertices . Combine these forces ( The sudden loss of pressure , the semi - toroidal flows , and adhesion ) and the net effect is a torsion force on the stream . The torsion force impels the fluid to twist and cohesion ( water molecules are kind of like tiny magnets and really want to stick together ) keeps the stream together . There you have it . Why your urine spirals instead of just flowing out like a garden hose . Urban forests play an important role in mitigating the urban heat island effect in cities. Trees provide shade and transpire water, which helps cool the air. The shade from trees blocks sunlight from reaching the ground and heating up surfaces like asphalt and concrete. The evaporation of water from tree leaves also requires energy and has a cooling effect. Studies have shown that temperatures in urban forests can be up to 5°C cooler than surrounding areas without trees. Urban forests are especially important for mitigating high temperatures during heat waves. As cities replace vegetation with man-made materials like asphalt that absorb and retain heat, urban heat islands develop. During heat waves, cities can become dangerously hot due to the urban heat island effect. By providing shade and cooling through evapotranspiration, urban forests help reduce temperatures and the impacts of heat waves in cities. They provide thermal comfort for city residents and help prevent heat-related illnesses. In addition to the direct cooling benefits from trees, urban forests also help reduce the need for air conditioning which further reduces urban temperatures. Air conditioners exhaust hot air outside, which contributes to higher temperatures in cities. By passively cooling buildings and providing shade, urban trees decrease the energy needed to cool indoor spaces. They improve the energy efficiency of cities and reduce emissions from power usage. Urban forests provide many environmental and social benefits in cities, including improved air and water quality, reduced noise pollution, increased property values, and more opportunities for recreation. However, their role in mitigating urban heat islands and cooling cities is one of the most important benefits, especially as climate change causes more frequent and intense heat waves. Protecting and expanding urban forests should be a priority for cities aiming to enhance resilience and sustainability. In summary, urban forests play an integral role in mitigating the urban heat island effect through shading and evapotranspiration. They help reduce temperatures during normal conditions and heat waves, improving thermal comfort and health in cities. Urban forests also decrease the need for air conditioning which further lowers temperatures in cities. By providing passive cooling, urban forests improve energy efficiency and sustainability in cities. They are a vital resource for urban heat island mitigation and building resilience to climate change.

In this paper, we present a synergic learning algorithm to address the task of indirect manipulation of an unknown deformable tissue. Tissue manipulation is a common yet challenging task in various surgical interventions, which makes it a good candidate for robotic automation. We propose using a linear approximate Q-learning method in which human knowledge contributes to selecting useful yet simple features of tissue manipulation while the algorithm learns to take optimal actions and accomplish the task. The algorithm is implemented and evaluated on a simulation using the OpenCV and CHAI3D libraries. Successful simulation results for four different configurations which are based on realistic tissue manipulation scenarios are presented. Results indicate that with a careful selection of relatively simple and intuitive features, the developed Q-learning algorithm can successfully learn an optimal policy without any prior knowledge of tissue dynamics or camera intrinsicextrinsic calibration parameters.

Recently, non-stationary spectral kernels have drawn much attention, owing to its powerful feature representation ability in revealing long-range correlations and input-dependent characteristics. However, non-stationary spectral kernels are still shallow models, thus they are deficient to learn both hierarchical features and local interdependence. In this paper, to obtain hierarchical and local knowledge, we build an interpretable convolutional spectral kernel network (CSKN) based on the inverse Fourier transform, where we introduce deep architectures and convolutional filters into non-stationary spectral kernel representations. Moreover, based on Rademacher complexity, we derive the generalization error bounds and introduce two regularizers to improve the performance. Combining the regularizers and recent advancements on random initialization, we finally complete the learning framework of CSKN . Extensive experiments results on real-world datasets validate the effectiveness of the learning framework and coincide with our theoretical findings.

The Difference Engine was intended to be a machine that could perform complex mathematical calculations and print out the results in the form of tables. It used a series of cog wheels and levers to perform arithmetic operations, and was driven by a series of punched cards similar to those used in early computers. The machine was designed to be able to calculate and print out tables of numbers with a high degree of accuracy, and was intended to be used in a variety of scientific and technical applications. Despite its advanced design, the Difference Engine was never widely used, due in part to the complexity of its construction and the difficulty of maintaining it. However, it remains an important early example of a machine that was designed to perform complex calculations, and is considered to be a precursor to the modern computer.

While technology that understands human emotions could potentially help teachers, the use of Facial Action Coding Systems to read students' expressions in the classroom raises some serious concerns. On one hand, such technology may allow teachers to better recognize when students are struggling, bored, or disengaged, so they can adapt their lesson accordingly. Identifying strong negative emotions could help teachers address bullying or other issues. And knowing when students truly understand or are excited by a topic may help guide instruction. However, this also creates risks to students' privacy and development. Constant monitoring of facial expressions could have a chilling effect and discourage natural emotional responses. Students may feel like they are under surveillance rather than in a nurturing learning environment. Wt also oversimplifies human emotion to think computers can definitively determine how someone feels based on facial cues alone. Moods and expressions are often more complex. Rather than focus so intently on measurements and data, effective teaching is better served by strong interpersonal skills. Teachers need to foster genuine connection and trust with students to really understand their wellbeing and progress. Technical solutions should only supplement, not replace, compassionate human judgment and care for students' overall growth. WF used without significant safeguards and oversight, this technology could compromise students' privacy and psychological safety at school. In many ways, students' emotional experiences are not for computers to analyze but for caring teachers, counselors, and parents to appreciate and address respectfully. Overall the risks seem to outweigh the potential benefits, suggesting this type of constant emotion scanning in classrooms is not presently advisable and requires much more research on effects and protection of student welfare before being implemented.

Participating in sports, clubs or other programs has been shown to improve attendance, time management skills and discipline all of which support higher grades. By taking activities away from C students, we risk removing these helpful influences from those who may need them most. A B average requirement could discourage C students from trying to improve if they feel they have no chance to participate no matter how hard they work. Instead of motivating higher achievement, it could backfire by lowering engagement from those most at risk of dropping out. A fairer policy may be to allow C students to play as long as they show effort towards raising their grades, such as meeting regularly with tutors or teachers for extra help. In conclusion, while the goal of supporting academics is admirable, an inflexible B average requirement is not the best way to achieve that. It risks harming dedication and motivation rather than improving outcomes. I believe with alternative assistance options, C average students can continue extracurricular involvement while still making progress on their grades. Please consider a more nuanced approach that supports all hardworking students. Thank you for considering my views. I hope this proposed policy can be reconsidered to keep opportunities available for dedicated students of all achievement levels. Sincerely, [Your name]

The Fugitive Slave Act, also known as the Fugitive Slave Law, was a federal law passed by the United States Congress in 1850 as part of the Compromise of 1850. The law required that individuals who claimed to be the owners of runaway slaves were entitled to a hearing before a federal commissioner to determine ownership. If the commissioner ruled in favor of the claimant, they were entitled to take possession of the runaway slave and return them to slavery. The Fugitive Slave Act was controversial and was opposed by many abolitionists and others who believed it was a violation of the rights of African Americans. It was ultimately repealed by the Thirteenth Amendment to the United States Constitution, which abolished slavery throughout the United States.

If you could invite anyone to speak at the Athena, who would you choose and why? If I could invite anyone to give a speech at the Athena speaker series on leadership, I propose George Washington. Now, you might have some reservations toward my decision. In our modern world, what we look for in our leaders is authenticity and openness, traits that allow us to see their humanity, and truly gain an appreciation for their accomplishments. Washington does not exactly fit that bill. Back in the battlefields of the war of independence-when opposing soldiers stared each other down and intimidation could inflict greater harm on an army than bullets-one of the qualities of a successful leader was the ability to lead by example: to stand firm with a straight face under a hail of fire and provide the steady reassurance that the troops needed to keep up the fight. Generals and statesmen who adopted this style of leadership, like George Washington, kept their inner thoughts and feelings hidden from their subordinates under an impenetrable shell. So when the modern citizens of America see glimpses of Washington's shell-the tale that Washington never told a lie or depictions of his stern face etched in marble-they dismiss the man as either one dimensional or a fabricated national mascot, and do not care to look any further. However, a look underneath that shell will reveal a human being marred by imperfections but gifted by a series of timeless leadership traits. Among these were the ability to learn from mistakes, the ability to adapt to new circumstances, and the drive to overcome almost impossible adversity. Most important to the revolutionary cause, Washington possessed the capacity to bring differing and independently minded men together for accomplishing a common goal. Even after the troops endured staggering defeats, months without pay, hunger, and cold, setbacks that could easily break apart professional European armies, Washington kept the continental army, and the entire revolutionary cause, from falling apart. We are in his infinite debt, as Washington was both the solitary man standing between an infant of a country and the unhinged might of a world empire. Only when we learn from his methods of leadership can we begin to repay him.

Seeking advice from multiple people when facing an important decision can provide significant benefits. By talking to different individuals, you gain access to a wider range of perspectives and life experiences. No single person can anticipate every aspect or ramification of a choice, but collectively others may highlight important factors that one advisor alone may miss. Getting input from more than one source also allows you to evaluate advice critically. Similar recommendations from various people lend credibility and make certain perspectives seem more reasonable. Contrasting advice allows you to analyze different positions and weigh potential positive or negative outcomes of each option more carefully. If one person advocates strongly for a course of action while others raise caution, you can consider both support for and risks of that choice. Multiple advisers may also balance or counteract any personal biases of a single recommender. Someone offering advice may favor a choice simply because it aligns with their personal experiences or preferences, without objectively considering other possibilities. Additional perspectives help expose such biases by providing alternative viewpoints that are untainted by certain preconceptions. Their less personally invested perspective forces deeper consideration of choices on their merits alone rather than through the lens of the original adviser's biases. Finally, getting counsel from more than one source leaves a decision more fully scrutinized from multiple angles before being made. A choice vetted and supported through discussion by multiple informed individuals provides greater confidence that important details were not overlooked during deliberation. Facing significant decisions, seeking a diversity of input lightens the load of responsibility to consider all factors comprehensively yourself. The collaboration of different minds addresses blind spots and results in a choice examined more thoroughly than you could alone. In the end, important choices carry lasting consequences that are best made after considering input from multiple trusted advisers who can provide fresh angles, balance individual biases, and ensure the decision receives comprehensive review from various perspectives. Seeking guidance from more than one knowledge source allows for wiser, well-rounded choices that incorporate outstanding viewpoints one person could not achieve in isolation.

The Phantom Face on Mars While some believe the Face on Mars is evidence of ancient extraterrestrial life, a closer examination suggests it is simply a naturally formed mesa. There are several reasons to think the Face is not an artificial construct, but rather a coincidence of light and shadow on the Martian surface. One key piece of evidence is how poorly defined the facial features actually are. Upon closer inspection with newer spacecraft like Mars Global Surveyor, the supposed "face" blurs into an indistinct hillside with no clear edges or defined structure typical of artificial objects. The lack of well-defined features makes it doubtful any intelligent being purposely carved a massive likeness into the rocky terrain. Additionally, similar mesas and buttes are commonly formed on Earth and Mars through natural erosional processes over vast timescales. Winds gradually wear away exposed rock in certain places more than others, eventually leaving hardened cap rock jutting up from softer sediments beneath. The Face plausibly resulted from ordinary wind erosion sculpting the surrounding rock into a form that superficially resembles a human face when viewed at a shallow angle from above. Perhaps most compelling is that NASA and other researchers have found numerous other landforms on Mars that resemble faces or structures from our perspective but are instead naturally occurring rock formations. Unless we are to believe aliens carved a vast "zoo" of forms replicating familiar patterns, the simplest explanation is that the Face, like these other cases, is a random product of natural geological forces, not artificial construction. Unless and until evidence of artificial materials or techniques is found, the prudent conclusion is that the famous Face is a trick of light and shadow on an ordinary Martian mesa. In conclusion, while the idea of an ancient alien message is intriguing to consider, careful scientific analysis indicates the Face on Mars is just a coincidence of natural landforms. Without clear evidence of artificiality, the default position remains that this famous Martian "face" is merely a naturally formed mesa exhibiting an optical illusion rather than extraterrestrial intervention when viewed from our vantage point on Earth. A prudent scientist must follow the evidence, not speculations, and in this case all evidence points to a natural origin for this phantom Martian face.

This statement implies that it is better to first collect data and then SSE that data to form a hypothesis or theory. While forming a hypothesis or theory without any data can lead to mistakes, it is not always an incorrect course of action. There is certainly a benefit to formulating a hypothesis or theory prior to collecting data. Doing so can fine researchers a starting point and a structure for collecting the necessary data. It can also help focus their research and provide direction to their study. By having a hypothesis or theory in place, researchers can also identify the most important pieces of data to collect and prioritize their resources accordingly. This can help sane time and resources which may Heine been used for collecting irrelevant data or may Heine been wasted in deaden research. For example, a researcher may study the impact of air pollution on public health. Before collecting any data, the researcher most form a hypothesis or theory. This can be something such as “long term exposure to air pollution increases the risk of respiratory diseases”. Having this hypothesis in place helps the researcher focus their research on gathering data related to air pollution, respiratory diseases, and the correlation between the two. The researcher can prioritize the most important pieces of data to collect and focus their resources on them. It is also important to note that the initial hypothesis or theory may be wrong or incomplete. In such cases, the data collected can be used to modify the hypothesis or theory and correct any mistakes. As long as the researcher is open to revising their hypothesis or theory based on the data, the risk of mistakes is minimized. In conclusion, theorizing before collecting data can be beneficial. It can help provide structure and focus to the research and prioritize the most important pieces of data to collect. However, it is important to remain open to revising the hypothesis or theory based on the data collected. Doing so can help avoid any mistakes and make the research more efficient.

However, I believe that this system is no longer effective in today's society. This would encourage presidential candidates to campaign across the country, rather than focusing solely on a select few states. Additionally, a popular vote system would eliminate the possibility of a candidate winning the presidency without receiving the most votes. In conclusion, I urge you to consider the benefits of a popular vote system for the U.S. presidential election. Hey there, fellow space enthusiast! I've heard you're convinced that the Face on Mars is a creation of extraterrestrial beings. While I understand the excitement around the possibility of alien life, I'm here to argue that the Face is, in fact, a natural landform. Let me show you why. Firstly, the Face on Mars is not a recent discovery. It was first observed in 1976 by NASA's Viking 1 Orbiter. If aliens had created it, wouldn't they have left some other signs of their presence? Like, maybe a Martian highway or a parking lot for their UFOs? But we haven't found any other structures like that. Secondly, the Face is not a perfect representation of a human face. It's more like a rough outline, with missing features and distorted proportions. If aliens were trying to communicate with us through a Martian Mount Rushmore, they wouldn't have made it so difficult to recognize. Thirdly, the Face is formed from natural geological processes. The article 'Unmasking the Face on Mars' explains that it's a result of erosion, weathering, and volcanic activity. The features we see are actually shadows and depressions, not actual structures. It's like when we see animals in clouds – our brains are wired to recognize patterns, even when they're not intentionally created. Lastly, the Face on Mars has changed over time. NASA's Mars Global Surveyor captured images of the Face in different lighting conditions, revealing how the shadows and depressions shift. If it were a constructed structure, it would remain the same, regardless of the angle of the sun. Evidence from the article that supports my claims includes the lack of other structures or signs of alien presence, the natural processes that formed the Face, and the changes we've observed over time. In conclusion, the Face on Mars is not a creation of aliens, but a natural landform that our brains are inclined to interpret as a face. I hope I've convinced you that the scientific explanation is the most plausible one. Let's keep exploring our celestial neighbor, but with a critical and open minded approach. Who knows what other wonders and mysteries Mars has in store for us?

An active learner is given a class of models, a large set of unlabeled examples, and the ability to interactively query labels of a subset of these examples; the goal of the learner is to learn a model in the class that fits the data well. Previous theoretical work has rigorously characterized label complexity of active learning, but most of this work has focused on the PAC or the agnostic PAC model. In this paper, we shift our attention to a more general setting - maximum likelihood estimation. Provided certain conditions hold on the model class, we provide a two-stage active learning algorithm for this problem. The conditions we require are fairly general, and cover the widely popular class of Generalized Linear Models, which in turn, include models for binary and multi-class classification, regression, and conditional random fields. We provide an upper bound on the label requirement of our algorithm, and a lower bound that matches it up to lower order terms. Our analysis shows that unlike binary classification in the realizable case, just a single extra round of interaction is sufficient to achieve near-optimal performance in maximum likelihood estimation. On the empirical side, the recent work in and (on active linear and logistic regression) shows the promise of this approach.

The Impact of Emerging Technologies on the Job Market The world is changing rapidly, and with it, so is the job market. Emerging technologies are disrupting businesses across industries, forcing companies to adapt and innovate in order to stay relevant. The impact of these technological advancements on the job market is significant, with some jobs becoming obsolete while new job opportunities are created. One of the most significant impacts of emerging technologies on the job market is automation. Automation refers to the use of machines and software to perform tasks that were previously done by humans. Automation has been embraced by many industries, especially manufacturing, as it increases efficiency and decreases costs. However, this also means that many jobs that involved repetitive tasks are at risk of being automated away. For instance, with the advent of robotics and artificial intelligence, factory workers who used to operate machines manually are now being replaced by robots. Another impact of emerging technologies on the job market is the creation of new job opportunities. As technology advances, new jobs are being created to support and manage these technologies. For example, with the rise of e-commerce, there is a growing need for professionals who specialize in data analytics, social media management, and cybersecurity. Similarly, with the development of artificial intelligence, there is a demand for machine learning engineers, data scientists, and software developers. Furthermore, emerging technologies are also changing the skills required for existing job roles. As technology becomes more integrated into our daily lives, workers must adapt to new tools and ways of working. For instance, sales representatives who used to rely on face-to-face interactions are now using video conferencing and online sales platforms to connect with clients. Similarly, office workers who used to type up documents are now using cloud-based collaboration tools like Google Docs. In conclusion, the impact of emerging technologies on the job market is complex and multifaceted. While some jobs are at risk of being automated away, new job opportunities are being created to support and manage these technologies. Additionally, existing job roles are changing as workers adapt to new tools and ways of working. It is crucial for workers to adapt to these changes by upskilling and reskilling themselves to stay relevant in the job market. Furthermore, policymakers must ensure that workers displaced by automation have access to training and support to transition to new job opportunities.

The country has now seen two consecutive quarters of declining growth, the usual definition of recession. Its vital oil industry has been hit by weaker global prices, according to the Nigerian Bureau of Statistics (NBS). But the government says there has been strong growth in other sectors. Outside the oil industry, the figures show the fall in the Nigerian currency, the naira, has hurt the economy. It was allowed to float freely in June to help kick-start the economy, but critics argued it should have been done earlier. The government, however, has found some positive news in the figures. "There was growth in the agricultural and solid minerals sectors.... the areas in which the federal government has placed particular priority," said presidential economic adviser Adeyemi Dipeolu. Nigeria, which vies with South Africa for the mantle of Africa's biggest economy, is also battling an inflation rate at an 11-year high of 17.1 in July. "A lot of Nigeria's current predicament could have been avoided," said Kevin Daly from Aberdeen Asset Management. "The country is so reliant on oil precisely because its leaders haven't diversified the economy. "More recently, they have tried, and failed, to prop up the naira, which has had a ruinous effect on the country's foreign exchange reserves and any reputation it might have had of being fiscally responsible." This economic recession comes as no surprise to millions of Nigerians. Many say they've never known it so tough. The slump in global oil prices has hit Nigeria hard. The government depends on oil sales for about 70 of its revenues. But critics say government policies made a bad situation even worse. The decision to delay devaluing Nigeria's currency meant many businesses struggled to get foreign currency to pay for imports, which had a cooling effect on the entire economy. The Development of Driverless Cars The introduction of driverless cars presents an interesting debate around both their potential benefits and drawbacks. While the article "Driverless Cars are Coming" discusses several advantages of these autonomous vehicles, a number of valid concerns remain that warrant serious consideration. On balance, I believe more research is needed before fully embracing their widespread adoption. Undeniably, driverless cars could solve many transportation issues we currently face. As the article notes, they may reduce traffic accidents caused by human error like distracted driving or drunkenness. By precisely following programming, autonomous vehicles could flow more efficiently on roads without incidents like speeding, reckless lane changes, or other dangerous behaviors. This alone could save thousands of lives annually according to some estimates. They also open up mobility for those unable to drive like the elderly or disabled. However, the technology is still in its early stages with many unknowns remaining. The article mentions how autonomous vehicles have struggled with unexpected scenarios on the road that their sensors did not anticipate. As the systems have yet to be fully tested over decades of real-world driving like human motorists, there is still a risk of accidents from unforeseen situations or software/hardware malfunctions. Public skepticism around disproportionate reliance on still-limited technology for life-and-death driving decisions is understandable. Moreover, widespread changes will disrupt many existing jobs across transportation sectors. In conclusion, while driverless cars hold promise in theory, more research and testing is prudent before widespread adoption. Prior to flashover , it 's very easy to determine the point of origin for a fire . Testing the area where the fire began can reveal accelerants . Visual inspection and other analysis can reveal deliberate attempts to fuel the fire ( like crumpled paper or other ' kindling ' ) . But after flashover ( the point when it goes from * a fire in a room * to * a room on fire * ) it 's a lot more difficult . Science is quickly catching up , but a lot of times " undetermined " is the best response they can give . It 's not like Hollywood where a fire investigator can walk into a gutted husk and tell within seconds that a fire was deliberately set ( at least , most of the time it 's not ) . But based on tests and demonstrations , the success rate is definitely improving . They use those test burns to collect data about the patterns that fire tends to follow . They can use those patterns to create computer models , then they can compare the results they see in a real fire with the expected results based on the information they have available ( floor plans , sources of ventilation , items contained in the room , ect ) and see if there are any discrepancies . Once they find a point of interest , they investigate until it is resolved , or until they conclusively prove that the evidence available is n't sufficient for a determination to be made .

Having a positive attitude is essential to success in life. It impacts not only how we interact with those around us, but how we perceive and overcome obstacles. A positive attitude allows us to approach every situation with optimism, rather than fear or pessimism, and this can make a significant difference in our lives. First, having a positive attitude can help us form better relationships with other people. When we view interactions with others in a positive light, we are more likely to understand their point of view and approach them with empathy and kindness. In contrast, a negative attitude can lead to conflict and further alienation from those we care about. Second, having a positive attitude can help us to approach problems in a constructive way. Rather than wallowing in self-doubt or giving up when faced with difficulty, a positive attitude encourages us to have faith in our own abilities and take action. A positive outlook enables us to realize that failure is not always the end of the story, and that often it is possible to learn and grow even in the face of adversity. Third, there is a big difference between positive and negative attitudes. A negative attitude causes us to focus on only the bad aspects of a situation, whereas a positive attitude allows us to see the potential for good even in the most challenging circumstances. This in turn can make it easier to find solutions to difficult problems rather than viewing them as insurmountable challenges. Lastly, having a positive attitude can help us to achieve our goals and be happier overall. When we approach life with a positive attitude, we start with the premise that we can achieve our goals and strive for success. We also open ourselves up to all of the potential for joy life has to offer, which can lead to a feeling of greater wellbeing. In conclusion, a positive attitude is essential to success in life. It affects our relationships, how we view and solve problems, and the likelihood of achieving our goals. Being positive leads to a happier, more fulfilled life.
